sampling_model.design: One target and \(J\) fixed donors are observed for \(n\) pre-treatment dates partitioned into \(L\) known proportional blocks; only the \(J\) untreated donors enter the \(T_1\) stable post-regime sample used for risk estimation.
sampling_model.units: The cross section is fixed. Pre-block and post-regime means obey the rank-\(r\) factor representation; \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=r\) then implies \(a_0\in\operatorname{col}(A)\) and \(d\in\operatorname{row}(A)\).
sampling_model.treatment: The target may be treated in the post period, but its post outcomes are excluded from the observed-data experiment for \(R_P\).
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is needed; identification is the row-span completion induced by the stable common-loading model.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate block means and donor post means by averages, \(\Sigma\) by pre-block-demeaned residual second moments, and their joint long-run covariance by block/HAC scores. The local optimality theorem uses the exact information in Gaussian block means and pre/post scatter statistics.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 establish sparse predictor selection consistency and a faster predictor-match mean-squared-error rate, without inference for population prediction risk along the tuning path.
Theorem 3.1 gives uniformly valid joint inference for a simplex optimizer and its functional at one fixed population objective through polyhedral-cone projection.
Theorems 1--2 and Theorem A give probability-guaranteed prediction intervals for a future synthetic-control counterfactual after propagating estimated-weight and post-regime errors.

Definition 1 restricts bands to those induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out randomly selecting among valid bands; Section 2.3 leads with weighted area; Theorem 2 is conditional on a generic objective, with low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation supplied specifically for weighted area.
Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 give Bayes--minimax duality for confidence sets under expected additive measure, and Theorem 2 solves a bounded one-dimensional shift family.
Theorem 2 proves convergence of a Monte Carlo approximation to a finite-prior minimax expected-measure confidence procedure.
Theorem 3.1 and its corollaries derive finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for scalar linear functionals over convex Gaussian regression classes.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 characterize ordinary-bootstrap failure and validate derivative-aware resampling for a fixed directionally differentiable functional.
Propositions 3.1--3.6 provide active-set degrees of freedom and information criteria for selecting synthetic-control penalties or predictor-weighting matrices.

body.tldr: Predictor weighting changes both the donor face and the future counterfactual performance of a synthetic control, yet current methods either tune one weight vector or report inference for one fixed constrained optimizer. This proposal identifies the entire population prediction-MSE graph from a block-stable fixed-rank panel, constructs an honest root-\(n\) same-panel band over the full predictor simplex, and solves the compact-local Gaussian decision problem for minimum worst-case expected maximum width by finite KKT-cell, conic-distance, and primal--dual linear programs with certified vanishing error. The central open step is an experiment-level Gaussian--Wishart transfer strong enough to preserve simultaneous coverage and expected maximum width for unrestricted randomized bands.

project_justification.gap: VivesiBastida2022PredictorSelection and PouliotXieLiu2026DegreesFreedom make predictor selection operational but do not attach an honest population-risk certificate to every candidate weighting. CanenSong2026SimplexWeight treats one fixed simplex objective. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands restricts attention to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and develops low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation for weighted area; other minimum-size confidence-set results treat scalar linear targets or additive set-measure losses. None addresses an unrestricted externally randomized max-curve-diameter decision for a piecewise-affine risk curve whose KKT face moves with the local query.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the observable graph \(G_P\) together with the exact compact-local price, measured by worst-case expected maximum interval width, of covering that graph when predictor and moment perturbations move donor faces on the same root-\(n\) scale.
project_justification.fill: The project combines row-span completion, a joint block-mean and covariance expansion, exact shifted-QP inversion, critical-cone curve geometry, certified finite primal and dual decision programs, and a matching local asymptotic lower-bound and attainment transfer from the actual observed Gaussian panel.

body.related_work: VivesiBastida2022PredictorSelection is the writing exemplar: its Introduction frames predictor weights as determinants of performance and interpretability, and Theorems 1--2 settle sparse support recovery and predictor-match rates rather than risk inference. CanenSong2026SimplexWeight, Section 2.5 and Theorem 3.1, is the closest constrained-inference method exemplar; its adaptive cone projection is used as the fixed-objective benchmark, while the present target couples a continuum of objectives and locally shifting slack. CattaneoFengTitiunik2021PredictionIntervals, Lemmas 1--2 and Theorems 1--2, supplies the uncertainty-decomposition discipline, but its target is a future counterfactual outcome rather than unconditional population MSE. FangSantos2019Directional, Theorems 3.1--3.2, explains why an ordinary bootstrap at a fixed nonsmooth map is unreliable; the local map here additionally changes with the predictor query. EvansHansenStark2005MinimaxConfidence, Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, and SchaferStark2009OptimalRegions, Sections 2--4, provide the Bayes--minimax and finite-program architecture for additive expected size. ArmstrongKolesar2018OptimalInference, Theorem 3.1, is the decision-theoretic writing exemplar for turning honesty into a computable efficiency benchmark, but its functional is scalar and linear. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands, Definition 1, restricts its band class to bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and rules out randomly selecting among valid bands. Its Section 2.3 leads with weighted area. Theorem 2 is conditional on a generic objective, but the paper supplies low-level sufficient conditions and a worked approximation specifically for weighted area. The present departure is stated independently: externally randomized measurable band actions, simultaneous maximum KKT-curve-diameter loss, and an observed-panel local minimax transfer. No strict numerical separation from Freyberger--Rai is asserted. PouliotXieLiu2026DegreesFreedom, Propositions 3.1--3.6, gives active-set information criteria for tuning; it informs the motivation for same-panel selection but does not implement the fixed-ridge objective studied here. The proposed certificate is for the displayed fixed-ridge quadratic simplex estimator and does not directly certify the different objectives implemented by Synth or SparseSC. Exact-pair searches through September 2026 found no published all-predictor population-MSE band or unrestricted randomized minimax-width solution for a moving-KKT synthetic-control risk graph. The March 2026 Martinez--Vives-i-Bastida preliminary work is adjacent research on synthetic-control predictor choice, but it is non-archival and is not used as a theorem-level comparator; the present target is the full population-risk graph and its unrestricted expected-maximum-width decision value.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The presolve derivations of the KKT atlas, the critical-cone risk map, and the finite acceptance-subset primal and dual have checkable algebra and an exactly solved binary hinge benchmark, but they are not treated as established. The proof must still close the uniform mixing CLT and HAC step, multiple-weak-face uniform remainder, measurable-band regularization, interval-certified computation, and especially the compact-local Gaussian--Wishart experiment transfer. Floating-point agreement at the hinge is diagnostic only. The global projection band is a validity construction only and is not asserted to be globally minimax; local optimality quantifies over the separate generic class \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{panel}}_{1-\alpha}\).
body.honest_scope: The global mixing-class band and the locally optimal Gaussian-neighborhood bands may be different procedures. Rank, donor count, predictor count, and block count are fixed; the rank is known and spectrally separated; the ridge is fixed positive; block means and the post regime are stable. The target is the displayed fixed-ridge quadratic simplex estimator, which is distinct from the objectives currently implemented by Synth and SparseSC; direct guarantees for those packages are not claimed. Unknown rank, growing dimensions, arbitrary singleton-date predictors, post-factor drift, shrinking ridge, and optimal inference for a corrected causal treatment effect are excluded. The linear-critical-cone reduction recovers ordinary scalar Gaussian interval inference on separated faces, and the explicit hinge shows that a moving boundary need not impose a positive extra width cost. The global parameter region is indexed by \(\Theta_n\) and the measurable observed-law map \(\theta\mapsto P_\theta\). Global minimaxity of \(C_n\) is not claimed; the local minimax comparison ranges over generic compact-locally honest sequences \(\widetilde C_n\). The March 2026 Martinez--Vives-i-Bastida preliminary work is treated only as adjacent non-archival research, not as an established theorem comparator.
